blocks.md: **I solve ONE part now; a smaller me handles the rest. Plus a smallest case answered directly.**

Two questions design ANY recursion: (1) What is the SMALLEST input I can answer instantly? (base) (2) Given the answer for n−1, how do I build the answer for n? (leap). Write those two lines and the function writes itself.

blocks.md: **Code placed BEFORE recursive call runs on the way DOWN; code AFTER runs on the way UP.** This single fact powers half of recursion problems.

revisionCard: Design = two lines: instant-smallest base + one-part-plus-leap
Before-call = downward order · after-call = unwind order
Branching recursion explodes exponentially when subproblems overlap
Leap of faith: assume smaller answer correct
Halving-power beats linear power (same DNA as binary exponentiation)
Stack depth = longest chain — watch inputs
